at the call’s start — no duration or size of its own
The whole session on one strip. Ticks are grey, amber for flagged and red for
failed — nothing else. Drag the brush (or Ctrl+wheel over the bars) to zoom; the
window is kept in the URL.
Any stretch of 60 s or more without network folds into a break mark with its
length, on the strip and as a thin row in the list. Default zoom is “Fit · gaps
compressed”; “Real time” shows the true scale.
One grey row per Bash / PowerShell / WebFetch / MCP call: tool, command, agent
and result, with the dashed span of the call. Its requests are the rows under
npm install with 214 requests stays collapsed by default with a density mark.
Groups outside the brushed window show their start at the edge (◂ 02:10, 05:15
Solid bar split into dns · connect · tls · wait · download when the Node script
tap measured them. A reused connection shows only wait + download.
Hatched bar: the duration is known but not its phases — only curl / wget / ssh /
scp / sftp seen by the command wrapper.
Python scripts record only the connect: a ◆ at that moment, no bar, “?” for
api.y.io was found in fetch.mjs but never seen connecting, so it has no time:
the tool call row only says “○ 1 inferred”; Requests lists it.
A folded or off-window group still shows its flags, so nothing suspicious hides
Only visible rows are drawn; the footer gives the row count. The legend explains
Clicking a bar or row opens the details pane: Seen by, timing, originating tool
call, bounded excerpt, Open turn ↗. No hover pop-over.
git, gh, docker, iwr, WebFetch, WebSearch, MCP: a ◐ at the tool call’s start,
“?” for duration and size. The dashed span on the group row is the tool call’s
time, never the access’s. Size and time are known only for
